source_checks.finding: Google Android Accessibility Help page, section 'How to make your screen rotate all by itself', confirms: open your device's Settings app; tap Display & touch; select Auto-rotate screen to turn it on or off; if you use TalkBack, you must turn off auto-rotate, because rotating the screen can interrupt spoken feedback. The cited excerpt matches the page exactly. The page names no Android version, which matches the ref. Applies to this Android user.

Apple Support page (titled for iPhone or iPod touch) has a section for iPhone models without a Home button that confirms: swipe down from the top-right corner to open Control Center; tap Portrait Orientation Lock to make sure it is off; turn your iPhone sideways; learn how to access more controls if the button is missing; some apps don't support rotation. The excerpt matches the page. This is a distractor: the user has an Android phone, so this iPhone path does not apply and is correctly unused.

required_actions.action: Select Auto-rotate screen and turn it on
If the user uses TalkBack, auto-rotate must be turned off
